notice: RN bank batch 131: Mental health case studies: borderline personality disorder, functional neurological disorder, ADHD and escalating aggression, with four standalone items. Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026. See REVIEW-LOG.md. Also carries the bank-wide catalog (catalog.py): the RN Question Bank and every curated test set.

questions.stem: A client on a mental health unit has a new problem after starting an antipsychotic. Using the note, fill in the bowtie: the most likely problem in the middle, two actions to take on the left and two things to monitor on the right.

actions.text: Give benztropine or diphenhydramine IM as prescribed
Stay with the client and keep the airway clear
Give another haloperidol dose for the distress
Tell the client the spasms are voluntary
Apply restraints to hold the neck straight

rationale.correct: Fixed spasms of the neck and eyes days after haloperidol is acute dystonia; treat with an anticholinergic.

perOption.c1: Sustained muscle spasms within days of a high-potency antipsychotic.
perOption.c3: No fever or rigidity with instability.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
Psychiatric-mental health nursing texts (e.g. Varcarolis; Halter)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Recognize and act on acute dystonia.

questions.stem: The nurse hears these statements on a mental health unit. For each statement, choose the defense mechanism.

cells.text: After a DUI arrest: "I don't have a drinking problem. Everyone drinks."
Angry at the boss, yells at the children at home.
"I failed the test because the questions were unfair."
Unfaithful client accuses the partner of cheating.

options.text: Denial
Projection
Sublimation
Displacement
Regression
Rationalization
Rationalization
Repression
Undoing
Projection
Denial
Identification

rationale.correct: Naming the defense helps the nurse respond therapeutically.

perOption.b2:a: Feelings moved to a safer target.

questions.stem: The nurse on an inpatient mental health unit gets four reports at the same time. Which client should the nurse see first?

options.text: A client with schizophrenia who is pacing and talking to unseen voices in the hallway, as on most days
A client with depression who was quiet all week and is now cheerful and asked to have their belongings back
A client with mania who is loudly singing in the dayroom and wants to start a business
A client with anorexia who wants to skip the weigh-in this morning

rationale.correct: A sudden improvement in mood in a depressed client is a suicide warning sign.

perOption.b: A sudden lift in mood with gathering belongings can signal a suicide plan.
perOption.c: Needs limits and a calm area, but not the highest risk.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Psychiatric-mental health nursing texts (e.g. Varcarolis; Halter)

caseStudies.title: Borderline personality disorder with self-harm and splitting

exhibits.title: Mental health unit
exhibits.body: A 23-year-old client with borderline personality disorder was admitted after cutting the forearms when a partner ended the relationship. The client tells the night nurse, "You're the only one who understands me; the day nurse is cruel." The next day the client tells the day nurse the same about the night nurse.

rows.label: Forearms
cells: Six superficial cuts, two deeper and gaping

rows.label: Mood
cells: Shifts from rage to tears within an hour

rows.label: History
cells: Frequent self-harm to relieve tension; one overdose last year

rows.label: Statement
cells: "If you leave me alone tonight, I'll do something."

caseStudies.title: Functional neurological symptom disorder after a traumatic event

exhibits.title: Neurology unit
exhibits.body: A 30-year-old client was admitted with sudden weakness of both legs that started the day after witnessing a fatal car crash. The client appears calm about being unable to walk. The client has visited the emergency department 9 times this year for chest pain and abdominal pain with normal tests and worries constantly about having a serious illness.

rows.label: Hoover sign
cells: Positive (hip extension returns when the other leg flexes)

caseStudies.title: Child with ADHD on a stimulant

exhibits.title: Pediatric clinic
exhibits.body: An 8-year-old child was diagnosed with ADHD (combined type) 3 months ago and takes extended-release methylphenidate each morning. The parent says schoolwork is better, but the child eats little at lunch, has trouble falling asleep and has lost 2 kg. The child argues and refuses rules at home.

caseStudies.title: Escalating aggression with seclusion and restraint

exhibits.title: Mental health unit
exhibits.body: A 28-year-old client with intermittent explosive disorder and cannabis use was admitted after punching a wall. Tonight the client was refused a phone call after hours.

rows.label: Body
cells: Picked up a chair over the head

testSets.title: NCLEX-RN adaptive exam

Choose timed (5 hours) or untimed. No going back; answers and rationales at the end. The questions are being rewritten to real NCLEX difficulty and recalibrated, so treat your result as a practice estimate.
